notes: A track that opens with music was being timed from the wrong place, so its words sat seconds away from the voice from the very first line.

The entrance was found by counting every frame a rise stayed above the bar instead of every attack. A drum kit holds a hit across two or three frames and a voice is one, so the opening beat alone reached the count a voice does.
On a song with a long musical opening that put the entrance at 0:00 and dragged the whole sheet forward with it.
An articulation is counted as an attack now, and the entrance is the first attack with more right behind it - a voice keeps articulating several times a second, which a beat cannot do.
Measured against a recording with a known entrance, the first line now lands on the voice, and on a song with a long intro the average error across the sheet fell from about 14 seconds to about 3.
A backing that only ever beats and never sings is left exactly as it was: the detector never invents an entrance, so those songs keep the lead-in they always had.
